clue.text: Become threadbare in the raw wind

indicators.note: to wind something is to twist and coil it, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment fraying because it is left out naked in a cold wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as the noun blowing on you, but it is the verb, as in winding a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that has worn thin from use is threadbare, so the phrasal verb matches the description.

clue.text: Cried when you and I had games lessons

blocks.note: you and I together are we
PT is physical training, school games lessons

explanation.surface: A child remembering tears shed during school sports.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the old school name for gym or games classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wept is the past tense of weep, so it is a direct synonym for shed tears.

clue.text: Produced vehicle almost second-hand

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a second-hand item has been used before

explanation.surface: A car dealer offering a nearly-used vehicle for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause something is to bring it about, the same as producing an effect or result.

clue.text: About to draw up final accounts for payouts

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards
final points to the last letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
taken as written, before it is turned
the last letter of accounts

explanation.surface: An accountant preparing to draw up end-of-year accounts for bonuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw up final accounts' looks like bookkeeping jargon, but it splits into three instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewards are sums paid out in return for something, so they are payouts.

clue.text: Accomplished lies are definitely beginning to work

indicators.note: putting letters to work sets them labouring into a new arrangement
the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the first letter of definitely

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that skilful lies are what really get results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like the verb linking subject and predicate, but its letters belong in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a plan or ambition is to achieve or accomplish it.

clue.text: Firm undertaking following money settlement

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for undertaking is placed behind the one for money

blocks.note: Co. is short for company, a firm
M is an abbreviation for money
a promise is an undertaking to do something

explanation.surface: A company's undertaking, given after cash is paid, settles a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following money' places the undertaking after M, while CO stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is an agreement reached by each side conceding something, a settlement of a dispute.

clue.text: Recover signal after short break

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: a rest is a break
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: Getting your strength back after a brief pause, once given the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost or in danger is to save or retrieve it, which is rescuing it.

clue.text: Normal to live for a drink

indicators.note: one thing given for another is exchanged, so the second item is swapped out for the first

blocks.note: average means normal or ordinary
to be is to exist, to live
taken as written; this letter is replaced

explanation.surface: Someone claiming it is perfectly ordinary to live for alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The A at the start of AVERAGE is replaced with BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any liquid served for drinking, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Crumble away, stored in zero degrees

indicators.note: what is stored in something sits inside it, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Food crumbling after being kept in a freezer at zero degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock or soil that erodes is gradually worn and crumbles away under weather or water.

clue.text: Determination shown by Belgian surrealist deserted by mate

indicators.note: being deserted by someone means they leave, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: René Magritte, the Belgian surrealist painter
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A painter whose resolve shows after his friend abandons him.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters M, A, T and E are scattered through the painter's name, not in one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, the same as determination to keep going.

clue.text: Panic sales surprisingly show a very slow rate

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A market report that panic selling is, oddly, happening only slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail's pace is an idiom for extremely slow movement, since snails crawl so slowly.

clue.text: Influenced mum to copy daughter

blocks.note: mum as in keep mum, be quiet: sh
to ape is to imitate
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother influencing her daughter, who copies her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but the adjective for silent, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape someone's views or life is to influence and mould them.

clue.text: Strongly committed to stick around southern Scottish island

indicators.note: something put around another encloses it, so the first word wraps about the rest

blocks.note: to paste is to stick
S is the abbreviation for southern
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone deeply attached to staying on an island in the south of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island off Mull in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey; the insertion splits the outer word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate person feels and acts with intense conviction, so is strongly committed.

clue.text: Rumble princess's disguise

blocks.note: Di, Princess Diana, with the possessive s
a cover is a disguise or false identity

explanation.surface: Seeing through a royal's disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumble' is British informal for finding someone out, not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumble a person or scheme, in British slang, is to discover what they are really up to.

clue.text: Extraordinary alliance between UN and America, semi-casual

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the word is kept and the other half is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
US is the United States
taken as written; only its second half is used

explanation.surface: A half-hearted pact between the United Nations and the US would be remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual is out of the ordinary, which is what extraordinary means.

clue.text: Friendly taxi takes a long way round

indicators.note: something that takes another in holds it, so one piece ends up inside the other
going round something encircles it, so the outer piece wraps the inner one

blocks.note: taken as written
a mile is a long way
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A friendly cabbie who drives a long way round to bump up the fare.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's sly taxi driver is a red herring: 'a long way' is the outer piece, and 'takes ... round' is one split instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable relations are good-natured and peaceable, so the word is a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Suitor is married, unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome means things went wrong, so the letters are out of their right order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad news for a lover: the object of affection already has a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courts someone, and an admirer is one who romantically pursues them.

clue.text: Voting is an elite con anyway

indicators.note: arranged any way means in any order at all, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cynic's view that democracy is just a trick played by the powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: An election is the formal process of choosing by ballot, so it is an act of voting.

clue.text: Bill, once separated, is able to sing well

blocks.note: first meaning: a request for payment
second meaning, once the word is split in two: having one's singing voice in good form

explanation.surface: A singer named Bill, once he went solo, found his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer reads IN VOICE, the phrase for a singer whose voice is in good form; 'once separated' tells you to break it.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a written bill for goods or services supplied.

clue.text: Type of calculation where 500+4 = 10+9, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the number's name is used

blocks.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
IV is 4 in Roman numerals
the equals sign is read as is
the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O
the first letter of nine, the number written as a word

explanation.surface: A puzzling sum that looks like nonsense arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The plus signs are just joins; the sum is read aloud piece by piece: D, IV, IS, IO, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Division is one of the four basic arithmetic operations, sharing a number into equal parts.

clue.text: Can be seen audibly to provoke

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the words are taken by their sound, not their spelling

blocks.note: what can be seen is in sight

explanation.surface: Something visible and heard that goads people.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or urge someone into action, the same as provoking them.

clue.text: Favour dubious free voting system first

indicators.note: something dubious is not straight or reliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order

blocks.note: PR is proportional representation
the letters of free rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic's preference for one questionable voting system over a supposedly free one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the voting system before the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer something is to like it better, to favour it over the alternatives.

clue.text: A type of order to announce the French uprising

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective: a postal order is a type of order

indicators.note: in a down clue rising up means the word is read from the bottom upward, backwards

blocks.note: to post a notice is to announce it
la is French for the

explanation.surface: An order issued to proclaim a French revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: A postal order is a British money order bought at a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal order is a kind of money order, so postal names that type of order.

clue.text: Disgraceful lad cons USA jockey

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and push about, so the letters are shifted into a new position

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A young jockey's swindle of America makes a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like the rider, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandalous conduct causes public outrage, which is what disgraceful means.

clue.text: Clothing bearing a quality mark?

blocks.note: kit is clothing or gear
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Clothes carrying a quality label.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kitemark is the British Standards quality symbol, shaped like a kite; the question mark admits that the answer is only part of the mark's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is the emblem of the British product-safety Kitemark, so it is loosely a quality mark.

clue.text: Held on to record secured by knight

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Kt is the abbreviation for knight
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A knight hanging on to a record he has acquired.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept is the past tense of keep, meaning retained or held on to.

clue.text: Complete introductions to the other teams at Lord's

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so each word gives up its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A full set of introductions for the visiting cricket teams at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Total as an adjective means entire or absolute, the same as complete.

clue.text: Advocate tea with politician before motion to abolish vehicle test

indicators.note: abolishing something does away with it, so those letters are struck out of the word

blocks.note: cha is slang for tea
an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: An MP over tea backs a parliamentary motion to scrap the car test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' is the verb here, to support a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to speak up for it, to advocate it.
